s923.content:
Floribert Bwana Chui was a young Congolese lawyer and a member of the Community of Sant’Egidio who worked as a customs inspector in Goma, on the border with Rwanda. He was offered large bribes to let a shipment of spoiled rice into the country, food that would have sickened the poor who ate it.

He refused, saying, “As a Christian, I cannot accept to sacrifice the lives of people.” In July 2007 he was kidnapped and murdered. He was beatified in 2025, a martyr of honesty.
s923.intercession: Bl. Floribert, pray for us, that we may never sell our conscience. Amen.

s924.content:
Helene Kafka was the daughter of a shoemaker in Vienna who became a Franciscan Sister of Christian Charity, taking the name Maria Restituta. She was a surgical nurse, quick, warm, and plain-spoken, loved by her patients.

When the Nazis took over Austria, she hung a crucifix in every room of the new wing of her hospital and refused to take them down. She was arrested in 1942, accused also of writing a poem against the regime, and beheaded in Vienna in 1943, the only religious sister in Greater Germany to be executed. She was beatified in 1998.
s924.intercession: Bl. Maria Restituta, pray for us, that we may never take down the cross. Amen.

s925.content:
Marcel Callo was a young printer of Rennes in France and a leader in the Young Christian Workers. During the Second World War he was sent to Germany for forced labor, where he found the other French workers in despair, and gathered them for prayer and Mass, and set up sports and a theater for them.

He was arrested by the Gestapo for being “too Catholic” and sent to the Mauthausen concentration camp, where he died, starved and sick, in 1945, at twenty-three. He was engaged to be married. He was beatified in 1987.
s925.intercession: Bl. Marcel, pray for all young workers. Amen.

s926.content:
Sára Salkaházi was a journalist in Hungary who joined the Sisters of Social Service. During the Second World War she and her sisters hid Jews in their houses in Budapest, saving about a hundred lives.

On December 27, 1944, the pro-Nazi Arrow Cross raided one of their houses. Sára was taken with the Jews she was sheltering to the bank of the Danube and shot. Before she died she made the sign of the cross. She was beatified in 2006, and is honored as Righteous Among the Nations.
s926.intercession: Bl. Sára, pray for us, that we may protect the persecuted. Amen.

s927.content:
Vilmos Apor was a baron of Transylvania who became a parish priest and then, in 1941, bishop of Győr in Hungary. He was known as the bishop of the poor, and during the war he spoke out against the persecution of the Jews.

In 1945, as Soviet troops took the city, he sheltered hundreds of women and children in the cellars of his palace. When drunken soldiers tried to take women away, he stood in their way and was shot, and he died a few days later, on Easter Monday. He was beatified in 1997.
s927.intercession: Bl. Vilmos, pray for us, and for all who defend the defenseless. Amen.

s928.content:
Aloysius Stepinac was a soldier in the First World War who became a priest and, at thirty-six, archbishop of Zagreb in Croatia. During the Second World War he intervened for persecuted Serbs, Jews, and others, and protested publicly against the racial laws and killings of the regime of the time.

After the war the Communist government of Yugoslavia put him on trial in 1946 and sentenced him to sixteen years of forced labor; he later lived under house arrest in his home village, where he died in 1960. Pope Pius XII named him a cardinal. He was beatified in 1998.
s928.intercession: Bl. Aloysius, pray for us, that we may be faithful under persecution. Amen.

s929.content:
Anacleto González Flores was a lawyer, teacher, and writer of Guadalajara in Mexico, a married father who led Catholic youth and workers. When the government of President Calles persecuted the Church in the 1920s, he organized peaceful resistance and became known as “the Mexican Gandhi.”

In 1927 he was arrested and tortured to reveal the whereabouts of a bishop. He refused, and before he was shot he forgave his executioners and cried, “I die, but God does not die! Long live Christ the King!” He was beatified in 2005.
s929.intercession: Bl. Anacleto, pray for us: long live Christ the King! Amen.

s930.content:
Carmen Rendiles was born in Caracas without a left arm, and wore an artificial one all her life. She joined the Servants of the Eucharist, and in 1965 founded in Venezuela the Servants of Jesus, who serve parishes, schools, and the poor.

She was known for her love of the Eucharist and of priests, her humility, and her humor about her disability. She was canonized in 2025, the first woman saint of Venezuela.
s930.intercession: St. Carmen, pray for us, and for all who live with disabilities. Amen.

s931.content:
Luigia Poloni was the daughter of a shopkeeper of Verona in Italy, who cared for the sick and elderly in the city’s poorhouse. With the priest Charles Steeb she founded in 1848 the Sisters of Mercy of Verona, taking the name Vincenza Maria.

The sisters nursed the sick in their homes and in hospitals, and cared for the victims of cholera. She died of cancer in 1855, and was canonized in 2025.
s931.intercession: St. Vincenza Maria, pray for the sick and those who care for them. Amen.

s932.content:
Joseph Allamano was a priest of Turin, the nephew of St. Joseph Cafasso, who for forty-six years was rector of the shrine of Our Lady of Consolation and renewed it as a place of prayer. Though he never left Italy, his heart was with the missions.

In 1901 he founded the Consolata Missionaries, and later the Consolata Missionary Sisters, who went first to Kenya and then around the world. He was canonized in 2024.
s932.intercession: St. Joseph Allamano, pray for us, and for all missionaries. Amen.

s933.content:
Elena Guerra was a woman of Lucca in Italy who founded the Oblates of the Holy Spirit to educate girls; St. Gemma Galgani was one of her students. She longed for the Church to rediscover the Holy Spirit, and wrote to Pope Leo XIII again and again, urging him to call all Catholics to pray to the Spirit.

Leo XIII listened, and in 1897 wrote an encyclical on the Holy Spirit and asked the whole Church to pray a novena before Pentecost every year. She is called the apostle of the Holy Spirit, and was canonized in 2024.
s933.intercession: St. Elena, pray for us: come, Holy Spirit, renew the face of the earth. Amen.

s934.content:
Élodie Paradis was a girl of Quebec who joined the Sisters of the Holy Cross, taking the name Marie-Léonie. She was sent to New York and to New Brunswick, where she saw how much the priests and the colleges needed help with their households.

In 1880 she founded the Little Sisters of the Holy Family, who cook, sew, and keep house for priests and seminaries, a humble and hidden work done with love. She was beatified in Canada by Pope John Paul II and canonized in 2024.
s934.intercession: St. Marie-Léonie, pray for us, that we may find God in humble work. Amen.

s935.content:
Álvaro del Portillo was a civil engineer of Madrid who met St. Josemaría Escrivá in 1935, joined Opus Dei, and became a priest. He was the founder’s closest collaborator for forty years, and worked at the Second Vatican Council.

After Escrivá’s death he led Opus Dei, first as its president and then as its first prelate and a bishop. He died in 1994, the day after a pilgrimage to the Holy Land, and was beatified in Madrid in 2014.
s935.intercession: Bl. Álvaro, pray for us, that we may be faithful in everyday things. Amen.

s936.content:
Concepción Cabrera, called Conchita, was a wife and mother of nine children in San Luis Potosí in Mexico, who was widowed young and raised her family alone. In the midst of an ordinary family life she lived a deep life of prayer, and wrote tens of thousands of pages on the spiritual life.

She inspired the Works of the Cross, among them the Missionaries of the Holy Spirit and the Religious of the Cross of the Sacred Heart of Jesus, devoted to the priesthood and to offering one’s life with Christ. She was beatified in 2019, the first Mexican laywoman to be beatified.
s936.intercession: Bl. Conchita, pray for all mothers and families. Amen.

s937.content:
Ceferino was the son of a Mapuche chief in Argentine Patagonia. He went to a Salesian school in Buenos Aires, hoping to become a priest and return to teach his people.

Sent to Italy to continue his studies, he fell ill with tuberculosis and died in Rome in 1905, at eighteen, a joyful and prayerful young man. He was beatified in 2007, the first indigenous Argentine to be beatified, and his shrine in Patagonia draws many pilgrims.
s937.intercession: Bl. Ceferino, pray for us, and for all indigenous peoples. Amen.

s938.content:
James Alberione was a priest of Alba in northern Italy who, praying before the Blessed Sacrament on the night between the nineteenth and twentieth centuries, felt called to serve the people of the new century. He saw that the press, and later film, radio, and television, could carry the Gospel to everyone.

He founded the Society of St. Paul and the Daughters of St. Paul, and a whole family of congregations and institutes, which publish books and media around the world. He was beatified in 2003.
s938.intercession: Bl. James, pray for us, and for all who work in the media. Amen.

s939.content:
Albertina Berkenbrock was a farmer’s daughter of German descent in the south of Brazil, a cheerful and devout girl who loved the Mass and taught the catechism to younger children.

When she was twelve, a farmhand who worked for her family attacked her in the fields; she resisted him, and he killed her. She was beatified in 2007 as a martyr of purity.
s939.intercession: Bl. Albertina, pray for all children, and protect them from harm. Amen.

s940.content:
Rosario Livatino was a young judge in Agrigento, Sicily, who prosecuted the Mafia with courage and was known for his honesty and his faith. In his diaries he wrote the letters “S.T.D.,” for Sub tutela Dei, “under the protection of God.”

In 1990, at thirty-seven, he was killed by Mafia gunmen on his way to work. Pope John Paul II called him a martyr of justice and indirectly of the faith, and he was beatified in 2021, the first judge to be beatified.
s940.intercession: Bl. Rosario, pray for us, and for all who serve justice. Amen.

s941.content:
Giuseppe Puglisi, called Don Pino, was a parish priest in Brancaccio, a poor neighborhood of Palermo controlled by the Mafia. He opened a center to keep children off the streets and away from the gangs, and spoke out against the Mafia’s hold on his people.

On his fifty-sixth birthday in 1993, he was shot dead by a Mafia gunman outside his home. He smiled at his killer and said, “I was expecting you.” He was beatified in 2013 as a martyr.
s941.intercession: Bl. Pino, pray for us, and for all children in danger. Amen.

s942.content:
Carlo Gnocchi was a priest of Milan who served as chaplain to the Alpine troops in the Second World War and went with them on the terrible retreat from Russia, where he promised dying soldiers to care for their children.

After the war he gave himself to the orphans and to the children maimed by mines and bombs, founding homes and rehabilitation centers for them. When he died he gave his corneas to two blind boys, at a time when this was not yet allowed in Italy. He was beatified in 2009.
s942.intercession: Bl. Carlo, pray for all wounded children. Amen.

s943.content:
Michał Kozal was the auxiliary bishop of Włocławek in Poland when the Germans invaded in 1939. He refused to flee and stayed with his people, and was arrested with many of his priests.

He was sent to the concentration camp at Dachau, where he encouraged and consoled the other prisoners, and died there in 1943, killed by a lethal injection. Pope John Paul II beatified him in 1987.
s943.intercession: Bl. Michał, pray for us, and for all who suffer for their faith. Amen.

s944.content:
Stefan Wyszyński was a priest who worked among Polish workers and hid during the Nazi occupation as a chaplain to the resistance. In 1948 he became archbishop of Warsaw and Gniezno and primate of Poland, and he led the Church through the long years of Communist rule.

He was imprisoned from 1953 to 1956. In prison he consecrated himself to the Virgin Mary, and afterward led the whole nation in a great novena of years leading to the millennium of Poland’s baptism in 1966. He was called “the primate of the millennium.” He was beatified in 2021.
s944.intercession: Bl. Stefan, pray for us, and for all who lead the Church through hard times. Amen.

s945.content:
Róża Czacka was a Polish countess who lost her sight at twenty-two. Instead of retreating, she traveled across Europe to learn how the blind were taught and cared for, and adapted Braille to the Polish language.

She founded the Franciscan Sisters Servants of the Cross, taking the name Elżbieta, and a school for blind children at Laski near Warsaw, which still serves them today. She was beatified in 2021.
s945.intercession: Bl. Elżbieta, pray for all who are blind, and for all who walk in darkness. Amen.

s946.content:
Maria Teresia Ledóchowska was a Polish countess who served as a lady-in-waiting at the court of Tuscany. Reading of the suffering of Africans under the slave trade, she gave up her life at court to work for Africa.

In 1894 she founded the Missionary Sisters of St. Peter Claver, who printed books, newspapers, and Bibles in African languages and supported the missionaries. She was called “the mother of Africa,” though she never went there. Her sister, St. Ursula Ledóchowska, was also a founder. She was beatified in 1975.
s946.intercession: Bl. Mary Theresa, pray for the Church in Africa. Amen.

s947.content:
Cecília Schelingová was a Slovak sister of the Sisters of Charity of the Holy Cross, known as Sister Zdenka, who worked as a nurse in the hospital at Bratislava. Under the Communist regime she helped a priest escape from the hospital where he was held, and was caught trying to free others.

She was tortured in prison and sentenced to twelve years. When she was gravely ill she was released, and she died in 1955 at thirty-eight. She was beatified in 2003.
s947.intercession: Bl. Zdenka, pray for all nurses and for all prisoners. Amen.

s948.content:
Anna Kolesárová was a girl of a Slovak village who, after her mother’s death, kept house for her father and brother, and went to Mass each morning.

In November 1944, as the front passed through her village, a Soviet soldier found the family hiding in their cellar and tried to force himself on her. She resisted, and he shot her in front of her father. She was sixteen. She was beatified in 2018 as a martyr of purity.
s948.intercession: Bl. Anna, pray for all young people, and protect them from harm. Amen.

s949.content:
Nikolaus Gross was a coal miner of the Ruhr in Germany who became a trade unionist and the editor of a newspaper for Catholic workers, and a father of seven children. He wrote against the Nazis even before they took power, and his paper was banned.

He took part in the circles that resisted Hitler, and after the plot of July 1944 he was arrested and hanged in Berlin in 1945. “If we do not risk our lives today,” he had said, “how can we justify ourselves before God and our people?” He was beatified in 2001.
s949.intercession: Bl. Nikolaus, pray for all workers and fathers. Amen.

s950.content:
Manuel Lozano, called Lolo, was a Spanish journalist from Linares who, as a young man in the Civil War, was imprisoned for carrying the Eucharist to others. At twenty-two he began to suffer from a disease that left him paralyzed and, in his last years, blind.

For twenty-eight years he wrote from his wheelchair, dictating when he could no longer see, articles and books full of joy, and founded a prayer group for the sick. He was beatified in 2010, the first lay journalist to be beatified.
s950.intercession: Bl. Lolo, pray for all journalists and for all who suffer. Amen.

s951.content:
Alberto Marvelli was a young engineer of Rimini in Italy and a leader of Catholic Action. During the Second World War, when Rimini was bombed again and again, he rode through the ruins on his bicycle bringing food and help to the homeless, and freed people from the trains taking them to German camps.

After the war he worked to rebuild the city and served the poor in public life. In 1946, on his way to a political meeting, he was struck and killed by a military truck, at twenty-eight. He was beatified in 2004.
s951.intercession: Bl. Alberto, pray for us, that we may serve others without counting the cost. Amen.

s952.content:
Benedetta Bianchi Porro was a girl of Romagna who had polio as a baby and went on to study medicine. While still a student she diagnosed her own illness, a disease that destroyed her nerves; she slowly lost her hearing, her sight, her movement, and almost all her senses.

Deaf and blind, she communicated through touch, and those who came to console her went away consoled. In her letters she wrote of having discovered that God is love, and of a joy her illness could not take away. She died at twenty-seven, and was beatified in 2019.
s952.intercession: Bl. Benedetta, pray for all who are sick and suffering. Amen.

s953.content:
Sandra Sabattini was a young woman of Rimini who joined the Pope John XXIII Community of Fr. Oreste Benzi and served drug addicts and people with disabilities. She studied medicine, hoping to be a doctor in Africa, kept a spiritual diary from the age of ten, and rose early each day to pray.

She was engaged to be married when she was struck by a car in 1984, and died three days later, at twenty-two. She was beatified in 2021, the first engaged woman to be beatified.
s953.intercession: Bl. Sandra, pray for all engaged couples. Amen.

s954.content:
Giuseppe Toniolo was an Italian economist, a professor at the University of Pisa, and a husband and father of seven. He worked out a Christian vision of economic life, in which work, the family, and the common good come before profit, and helped prepare the Church’s social teaching.

He founded Catholic social weeks and helped bring Catholics into public life, and he prepared the way for the founding of the Catholic University of the Sacred Heart in Milan. He was beatified in 2012.
s954.intercession: Bl. Giuseppe, pray for all who work for a just economy. Amen.

s955.content:
Teresio Olivelli was a young lawyer of Pavia who at first believed in Fascism, then turned against it. He served as an officer on the Russian front in the Second World War, helping wounded soldiers in the retreat, and afterward joined the Catholic resistance and wrote the “Prayer of the Rebel.”

Arrested and sent to the camps, he shared his food with others and defended the weak. In the camp at Hersbruck he threw himself in front of a young prisoner who was being beaten, and was beaten to death himself in 1945. He was beatified in 2018.
s955.intercession: Bl. Teresio, pray for us, that we may defend the weak. Amen.

s956.content:
Armida Barelli was a woman of Milan who gave her life to the formation of young women, founding the Women’s Youth of Catholic Action, which grew to hundreds of thousands of members.

With Fr. Agostino Gemelli she founded the Catholic University of the Sacred Heart in Milan, raising the money for it from ordinary Catholics across Italy, and she cofounded the Missionaries of the Kingship of Christ, a secular institute. She was beatified in 2022.
s956.intercession: Bl. Armida, pray for all young women. Amen.

s957.content:
Ján Havlík was a Slovak seminarian of the Congregation of the Mission, the Vincentians, when the Communist regime of Czechoslovakia closed the seminaries. He went on studying in secret.

In 1951 he was arrested and sentenced to forced labor in the uranium mines, where he was beaten and worn down, and still wrote of his love for Christ. He was released in 1962, broken in health, and died three years later, at thirty-seven. He was beatified in 2024 as a martyr.
s957.intercession: Bl. Ján, pray for all seminarians and all who are persecuted. Amen.

s958.content:
Max Josef Metzger was a German priest who served as an army chaplain in the First World War and came home a convinced worker for peace. He founded a peace league and a religious community, and was one of the first Catholics to work for the unity of Christians.

Under the Nazis he was arrested several times. In 1943 he wrote a memorandum for a peaceful, democratic Germany after the war; he was betrayed, sentenced to death, and beheaded in 1944. He was beatified in 2024.
s958.intercession: Bl. Max Josef, pray for peace and for the unity of Christians. Amen.

s959.content:
Rosa Sgorbati was an Italian Consolata Missionary Sister, Sister Leonella, who spent more than thirty years in Kenya training nurses, and then went to Mogadishu, in war-torn Somalia, to found a school of nursing at the only hospital there.

In September 2006 she was shot in the back as she crossed the road from the hospital to the convent, together with her Muslim bodyguard, who died trying to protect her. Her last words were “I forgive, I forgive, I forgive.” She was beatified in 2018.
s959.intercession: Bl. Leonella, pray for us, that we may forgive. Amen.

s960.content:
Odoardo Focherini was an insurance man and journalist of Carpi in Italy, the father of seven children, and a leader of Catholic Action. During the Second World War he organized a network that gave false papers to Jews and helped more than a hundred escape to Switzerland.

He was arrested in 1944 and died in the concentration camp at Hersbruck, saying that he offered his life for his family, for the Church, and for his country. He is honored as Righteous Among the Nations, and was beatified in 2013.
s960.intercession: Bl. Odoardo, pray for us, that we may protect the persecuted. Amen.

s961.content:
Bronisław Markiewicz was a Polish priest who went to Turin in 1885 to join St. John Bosco, who received him into the Salesians. Returning to Poland, he gave himself to poor and abandoned boys in the village of Miejsce Piastowe, giving them a home, schooling, and a trade.

He founded the Congregation of St. Michael the Archangel, whose priests and sisters carry on his work with the young. He was beatified in 2005.
s961.intercession: Bl. Bronisław, pray for all abandoned children. Amen.

s962.content:
Teresa Bracco was a farmer’s daughter in the hills of Piedmont in Italy, who worked in the fields and walked each morning to Mass.

In August 1944, during the war, German soldiers raided her village. One of them dragged her into the woods and tried to force himself on her; she resisted, and he strangled and shot her. She was twenty. She was beatified in 1998 as a martyr of purity.
s962.intercession: Bl. Teresa, pray for all young women, and protect them from violence. Amen.
